description: We are Team Four the Plot: Riya, Diya, Saadhya and Aaliyah. Our project, DUSTBOUND, is an interactive space documentary narrated by two imagined storytellers: Dusty, the voice of Mars, and Selene, the voice of the Moon. It tells the stories of NASA machines left behind on Mars and the Moon, using real NASA science and imagery.
summary: Space exploration leaves machines, experiments and stories behind, and complex archives can overwhelm young learners. DUSTBOUND turns these into a guided journey. Dusty introduces four Mars rovers (Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance), and Selene explains the six Apollo landings and the hardware left on the Moon. Learners can also play six mission games and a "Which rover are you?" quiz. All missions, dates and discoveries link to NASA sources. The site is built with HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript and hosted on Netlify.
details:
What it does and how it works
DUSTBOUND is an interactive website that tells the stories of NASA machines left behind on Mars and the Moon. A visitor chooses a planetary journey. On Mars, the guide Dusty introduces the Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance rovers, and on the Moon, the guide Selene explains the six Apollo landings and the equipment left on the surface. Each chapter pairs a short story with a “NASA Record” box that gives the real facts and a link to the source. Visitors can then play six mission games and take a “Which rover are you?” quiz, earning Star Points and achievements.

Benefits and intended impact
Space archives are often too technical for young learners. DUSTBOUND turns them into a short, friendly story, so students aged 10 to 18 and their teachers can learn real space history without a science background. We want to support STEM accessibility, spark youth curiosity and give retired space hardware the recognition it deserves.

Tools and technologies
HTML5 for structure, CSS3 for design, JavaScript for interactivity and games, and Netlify for hosting, so anyone can open it with a link. All content comes from NASA resources: NASA Science (Mars missions, Ingenuity and the Moon), the NASA Apollo Program pages, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission, and NASA’s imagery with credits.

How it is creative
Instead of a fact list, two imagined narrators, Dusty and Selene, speak for the machines themselves. Learning is built around play, and visitors can read in silence or turn the narration on.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: every fact is checked against NASA sources and credited.
  • Honesty: illustrations are labeled as illustrations, and findings are described carefully (for example, “evidence of habitability, not proof of life”).
  • Accessibility: narration controls, a silent-reading option and image descriptions.
  • Fit with the challenge: we focus on retired and left-behind hardware, and present the active rovers as the next chapter.
  • Audience: short story chunks and games that suit students.
